method: Innings pitched are entered in baseball notation, where .1 is one out and .2 is two outs, so 6.2 means 6 2/3 innings; the page converts the entry to a whole number of outs (whole innings x 3 plus the fraction digit) and calculates from that, so no float fraction is rounded twice. Innings pitched must be greater than zero and at most 999 innings, and the fraction digit may only be 0, 1 or 2. Earned runs, hits allowed, walks, strikeouts and home runs allowed are whole numbers from 0 to 20,000. Earned run average is 9 x earned runs / innings pitched, written as 27 x earned runs / outs. WHIP is (hits + walks) / innings pitched, written as 3 x (hits + walks) / outs. Strikeouts, walks and home runs per nine scale the same counts by 27 / outs, and the strikeout-to-walk ratio is strikeouts / walks, shown as a dash when there are no walks because the ratio is undefined. Every rate is rounded half away from zero to two decimals, which is the precision the page displays. The tool models one pitcher's line as entered: it does not separate inherited runners, unearned runs, park or league effects, opponent strength or era, and it makes no projection. Everything is calculated in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Major League Baseball official rules, Rule 9.22: earned run average is earned runs multiplied by nine and divided by innings pitched
Official scoring convention: innings pitched are counted in thirds, written .1 for one out and .2 for two outs
WHIP is walks plus hits divided by innings pitched, a widely used rate statistic rather than an official MLB statistic
